main_text.p: calgationes fanat,& maximè candidi. Laudatur & gallinæ fel,præcipueque adeps con-Adeps.tra pustulas in papillis,adiuuatq; mirifice ruptas oculorum tunicas admixto lapide hæmatite.

Fimum gallinaceorum,sed rubrum, lufcis-Fimum.efis[?] illinendum suadent, morsisque à rabido canè exaceto : fimum quoque gallinarum candidum in veteri oleo corneisque pyxidibus afferuare solent ad oculorum albugines, miscetur autem cum rosacea, fœniculacea, vel oui albumine. Earundem fimum candi-dam hissopo aut mulso decoctum, venena fungorum[?] astringit, inflationes itè & strangulationes,quod mirari subit, si enim id fimū gustauerit aliud animal, torminibus afficitur & inflationibus. Verrucas quoq; pellit cum oleo & nitro fimum gallinaceorum.
Non omittam hîc mysterium naturæ.Cor. Nam cor è viuente gallina exectum dextreq; coxæ palpitans adhuc alligatum partum dif-ficilem accelerat.

Ventriculi gallinaceorū membrana, quæVentriculus. in coctionibus abiici solet, vino trita auib[?] purulentis calida infunditur, sic & gallinarū adeps: eadem ficcata & potioni inspersa stomachicis, pectoris destillationibus, humidæque medetur tussi. Gallinaceorum iecuras-fum cum prædicta ventriculi membrana admisto papaueris succo dysentericis ꝑdestvé-trisq; malis.

page.notes: The right margin notes are Adeps, Fimum, Cor and Ventriculus; the last is partly cut off and read as "culus". The marginal note "Ventriculus" reads partly as "Ventri-" at the line end. The word "dy(entericis" is read as "dysentericis". Several words near the lower part of the page are doubtful: "efis", "fungorum", "auib", and "pdestvé" which is read as ꝑdestvé. The catchword "De" stands at the foot.
